flows.name: A job's life
flows.description: One job from the moment it is posted to the moment GitHub's record is checked against what its agent claimed.

steps.text: Posted: a session posts a job over MCP. The Worker checks the caller's grant, picks the model, signs the body and stores the job.
Claimed: an agent claims it. The Worker verifies the body's signature first and records who holds the job.
Worked: the agent works on one branch of one repo.
Blocked: at a push, a deploy, a secret or a merge the agent stops. The job waits with the exact command a person or the signed policy must approve, and resume hands it back.
Pull request: the pull request opens through Capsid's GitHub App, and CI runs on it.
Merged: the five-minute tick merges a pull request whose CI is green on its exact head under the signed auto-merge policy, or the session that opened it merges it on green.
Deployed: the merge to master runs CI on GitHub Actions, which deploys the Worker.
Verified: CI's live gate reads the Worker's /health and checks it reports the commit that was merged.
Claims checked: when the job completes, the Worker reads the pull request, its commits and CI from GitHub and records each claim beside what GitHub says.

flows.name: The nightly backup
flows.description: Once a day the Worker copies the whole store to R2, keeps a graduated set of copies, trims old history only once a copy holds it, and the watcher checks that the copy kept off the account is fresh.

steps.text: Dumped: at 09:00 UTC a daily cron in the Worker dumps every table to R2 with d1-dump, one JSON file each plus the schema.
Marked complete: a completion marker is written last, and only when the dumped tables match the ones the migrations create. A run without it is never counted as a backup.
Mirrored: every document body is written beside the dump as plain markdown, one file per document.
Pruned: the newest complete run of each of the last 14 days, 8 weeks and 6 months is kept, and every other run is deleted whole. The newest complete run is never deleted.
Trimmed: document versions older than 90 days and audit rows older than 180 are pruned, after the dump, so every pruned row is in a kept copy.
Stamped: the run records its success, and /health warns once that stamp is more than 26 hours old.
Watched: every half hour the watcher reads the newest copy kept off the Cloudflare account and files a finding once it is more than 36 hours old.

flows.name: Publishing a post
flows.description: A post goes from a private draft in Carrel to a live page on dustinedwards.info, through the one contract every site speaks, with the site deciding what may go live.

steps.text: Drafted: the writer works in Carrel's editor, which autosaves a working draft only that person can see.
Previewed: Carrel shows the site's own render of the draft in a sandbox, with the checks' flags and any reviewer's beside it.
Saved: an Editor or the Owner saves the draft to the site, naming the version it replaces. The site refuses a stale one, so nobody overwrites a newer save.
Published: only the Owner publishes, and a first publish asks for confirmation. The site's own publish policy decides, so there is one authority.
Or by instruction: the Owner's AI session may publish through the MCP door, never while a flag is open. It sends no text, so only the saved version goes live, and Dustin is emailed an unpublish link.
Recorded: Carrel indexes the live post, records who published it (an AI session by its client name) and clears the draft that was sent.
Watched: every 15 minutes Carrel runs site-api's conformance suite against the site and emails when its state changes.
